title: Ensure ROS 2 nodes run with SROS2 security enforced
description: Without SROS2, DDS traffic between ROS 2 nodes is unauthenticated and unencrypted, so anyone on the network can publish commands or read sensor data. Security is switched on per process by ROS_SECURITY_ENABLE=true, ROS_SECURITY_STRATEGY=Enforce (Permissive silently falls back to insecure) and ROS_SECURITY_KEYSTORE. The audit inspects /proc/<pid>/environ of running processes whose environment contains ROS_DISTRO (run as root) and fails if none is found or any lacks these settings. Run tmaegis from a shell that has not sourced the ROS setup script.
reference: CIS-style ROS 2 hardening guidance - SROS2 DDS security (no CIS benchmark section; verify against your hardening standard)

remediation.command: Create a keystore and enclaves (ros2 security create_keystore /etc/ros/keystore; ros2 security create_enclave /etc/ros/keystore /<ns>/<node>), then set ROS_SECURITY_KEYSTORE=/etc/ros/keystore, ROS_SECURITY_ENABLE=true and ROS_SECURITY_STRATEGY=Enforce in the launch environment (systemd unit Environment= or launch file) of every node and restart them.

title: Disable rosmaster listening on all interfaces by default
description: rosmaster is the handshaking server responsible for connecting publishers to subscribers and vice-versa. By default it listens on all interfaces on a given machine, including external interfaces. This greatly increases attack surface area, and is only required if one is using distributed computing (where multiple machines are running ROS and need to connect to the same master). The audit requires the ROS master port 11311 to listen only on loopback (ss); when rosmaster is not running it requires every running ROS 1 process to have ROS_HOSTNAME (or ROS_IP) set to localhost. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.10 Disable rosmaster listening on all interfaces by default

audit.command:
command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
l=$(ss -Hltn 'sport = :11311' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
if [ -n "$l" ]; then bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$l" | awk '{print $4}' | grep -Ev '^(127\.[0-9.]+|\[::1\]|::1):11311$')
  [ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || echo "rosmaster listens on: $(printf '%s ' $bad)"; exit 0; fi
bad=0; for e in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do env=$( (tr '\0' '\n' < "$e") 2>/dev/null ) || continue
  case "$env" in *ROS_DISTRO=melodic*|*ROS_MASTER_URI=*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  h=$(printf '%s\n' "$env" | sed -n 's/^ROS_HOSTNAME=//p;s/^ROS_IP=//p' | head -n 1)
  case "$h" in localhost|127.0.0.1|::1) ;; *) echo "pid ${e#/proc/}: ROS_HOSTNAME/ROS_IP=${h:-unset}"; bad=1 ;; esac
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Ensure the ROS_HOSTNAME environment variable is set to localhost, thereby ensuring rosmaster only listens on loopback and isn't accessible on the network. One can cover most user session services and applications by adding the following line to /etc/environment: ROS_HOSTNAME="localhost" Note that this will not cover systemd system units. If a unit is being created that runs rosmaster (e.g. roscore or roslaunch), make sure this environment variable is set by utilizing Environment=, EnvironmentFile=, or similar.

title: Ensure SSH root login is disabled
description: The PermitRootLogin parameter specifies if the root user can log in using ssh. The default is no. The audit requires PermitRootLogin no. The audit reads the effective sshd configuration (sshd -T, root). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.10 Ensure SSH root login is disabled

audit.command:
command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(sshd -T -C user=root -C host="$(hostname)" -C addr="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)" 2>/dev/null) || out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'tolower($1)=="permitrootlogin"{print tolower($2); exit}')
case "$v" in no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "PermitRootLogin ${v:-unset}" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter as follows: PermitRootLogin no

title: Ensure password fields are not empty
description: An account with an empty password field means that anybody may log in as that user without providing a password. The audit requires every account in /etc/shadow to have a non-empty password field. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.1 Ensure password fields are not empty

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
u=$(awk -F: '($2 == "") {print $1}' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$u" ] && echo compliant || echo "accounts without password: $(printf '%s ' $u)"

remediation.guidance: If any accounts in the /etc/shadow file do not have a password, run the following command to lock the account until it can be determined why it does not have a password: # passwd -l <username> Also, check to see if the account is logged in and investigate what it is being used for to determine if it needs to be forced off.

title: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
description: Any account with UID 0 has superuser privileges on the system. The audit requires root to be the only UID 0 account. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.3 Ensure root is the only UID 0 account

audit.command:
u=$(awk -F: '($3 == 0) {print $1}' /etc/passwd) || exit 1
[ "$u" = root ] && echo compliant || echo "UID 0 accounts: $(printf '%s ' $u)"

remediation.command: Remove any users other than root with UID 0 or assign them a new UID if appropriate.

title: Ensure ROS 2 discovery is limited to the local host
description: By default ROS 2 multicasts DDS discovery to the whole subnet, exposing every topic and service to other machines. Humble/Iron use ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1; Jazzy and later use ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST (or OFF). The audit inspects /proc/<pid>/environ of running processes containing ROS_DISTRO (run as root) and fails if none is found or any process allows wider discovery. Multi-host robots that must discover peers should instead use SUBNET with ROS_STATIC_PEERS and SROS2, and document the exception.
reference: CIS-style ROS 2 hardening guidance - Restrict DDS discovery scope (no CIS benchmark section; verify against your hardening standard)

audit.command:
found=0; bad=0
for e in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do
  env=$( (tr '\0' '\n' < "$e") 2>/dev/null ) || continue
  case "$env" in *ROS_DISTRO=*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  found=1
  pid=${e#/proc/}; pid=${pid%/environ}
  if printf '%s\n' "$env" | grep -Eqx 'ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=(LOCALHOST|OFF)'; then continue; fi
  if printf '%s\n' "$env" | grep -qx 'ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1' && ! printf '%s\n' "$env" | grep -q '^ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE='; then continue; fi
  echo "pid $pid: discovery not limited to localhost"; bad=1
done
[ "$found" -eq 1 ] || { echo "no running ROS 2 processes found"; exit 1; }
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Jazzy+: set ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST (optionally ROS_STATIC_PEERS for known peers). Humble/Iron: set ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1. Apply in the launch environment of every node and restart them.

title: Ensure SROS2 governance and permissions enforce encryption and least privilege
description: Enabling SROS2 is not sufficient on its own: the signed governance document decides whether unauthenticated participants are allowed and whether traffic is encrypted, and per-enclave permissions decide which topics each node may publish or subscribe. These documents are site specific, so this is a review item.
reference: CIS-style ROS 2 hardening guidance - SROS2 access control policy (no CIS benchmark section; verify against your hardening standard)

audit.command: In the keystore ($ROS_SECURITY_KEYSTORE/enclaves/governance.xml) confirm allow_unauthenticated_participants=false, enable_join_access_control=true and rtps/discovery/liveliness protection_kind ENCRYPT. For each enclave permissions.xml, confirm publish/subscribe grants are limited to the topics that node needs (no "*" wildcards). Check that private/ key files are readable only by the service account (mode 600) and the CA private key is kept off the robot.

remediation.command: Write a policy file and regenerate permissions (ros2 security create_permission <keystore> <enclave> policy.xml), edit governance.xml for ENCRYPT and re-sign it with the keystore CA, copy only the needed enclaves to the robot and restart the nodes.

title: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled
description: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. A cramfs image can be used without having to first decompress the image. The audit requires the cramfs module to be unloaded and blocked (modprobe -n -v reports install /bin/true). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.1 Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled

audit.command:
command -v modprobe >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
grep -qw '^cramfs' /proc/modules 2>/dev/null && { echo 'cramfs is loaded'; exit 1; }
cfg=$(modprobe -n -v cramfs 2>&1)
case "$cfg" in *'install /bin/true'*|*'install /bin/false'*|*'not found'*) echo compliant; exit 0 ;; esac
modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -Eq '^\s*install\s+cramfs\s+/bin/(true|false)' && echo compliant || echo 'cramfs can be loaded'

remediation.guidance: Edit or create a file in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory ending in .conf Example: vi /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf and add the following line: install cramfs /bin/true Run the following command to unload the cramfs module: # rmmod cramfs

title: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
description: The nodev mount option specifies that the filesystem cannot contain special devices. The audit requires the nodev mount option on /tmp when it is a separate mount (findmnt); not applicable otherwise. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.3 Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition

audit.command: if ! findmnt -kn /tmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo compliant; elif findmnt -kn -o OPTIONS /tmp | tr ',' '\n' | grep -qx -- nodev; then echo compliant; else echo '/tmp is mounted without nodev'; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/fstab file and add nodev to the fourth field (mounting options) for the /tmp partition. See the fstab(5) manual page for more information. Run the following command to remount /tmp : # mount -o remount,nodev /tmp OR If systemd tmp.mount is configured: Edit /etc/systemd/system/local-fs.target.wants/tmp.mount to add nodev to the /tmp mount options: [Mount] Options=mode=1777,strictatime,noexec,nodev,nosuid Run the following command to remount /tmp : # mount -o remount,nodev /tmp

title: Ensure sticky bit is set on all world-writable directories
description: Setting the sticky bit on world writable directories prevents users from deleting or renaming files in that directory that are not owned by them. The audit searches local filesystems for world-writable directories without the sticky bit and requires none. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.21 Ensure sticky bit is set on all world-writable directories

audit.command:
command -v findmnt >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
mps=$(findmnt -rn -l -o TARGET,FSTYPE | awk '$2 !~ /^(nfs|nfs4|cifs|smb3|smbfs|fuse|proc|sysfs|tmpfs|devtmpfs|devpts|cgroup|cgroup2|pstore|securityfs|debugfs|tracefs|configfs|bpf|mqueue|hugetlbfs|autofs|binfmt_misc|efivarfs|overlay|squashfs|nsfs|ramfs|fusectl|rpc_pipefs)$/ {print $1}')
out=$(for m in $mps; do find "$m" -xdev -type d \( -perm -0002 -a \! -perm -1000 \) -print 2>/dev/null; done | sort -u | head -n 50)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || { printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo 'world-writable directories without the sticky bit'; }

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the sticky bit on all world writable directories: # df --local -P | awk '{if (NR!=1) print $6}' | xargs -I '{}' find '{}' -xdev -type d \( -perm -0002 -a ! -perm -1000 \) 2>/dev/null | xargs -I '{}' chmod a+t '{}'

title: Ensure sudo is installed
description: sudo allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user, as specified by the security policy. The invoking user's real (not effective) user ID is used to determine the user name with which to query the security policy. The audit requires the sudo or sudo-ldap package (dpkg-query). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure sudo is installed

audit.command:
command -v dpkg-query >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1

remediation.guidance: Install sudo using the following command. # apt install sudo OR # apt install sudo-ldap

title: Ensure sudo commands use pty
description: sudo can be configured to run only from a psuedo-pty The audit requires "Defaults use_pty" in /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d/*. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.2 Ensure sudo commands use pty

audit.command: grep -Pqs -- '^\s*Defaults\s+([^#]+,\s*)?use_pty(,\s*\S+\s*)*(\s+#.*)?$' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d/* && echo compliant || echo 'Defaults use_pty is not set'

remediation.guidance: edit the file /etc/sudoers or a file in /etc/sudoers.d/ and add the following line: Defaults use_pty

title: Ensure sudo log file exists

reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.3 Ensure sudo log file exists

remediation.guidance: edit the file /etc/sudoers or a file in /etc/sudoers.d/ and add the following line: Defaults logfile="<PATH TO CUSTOM LOG FILE>" Example Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo.log"

title: Ensure AIDE is installed
description: AIDE takes a snapshot of filesystem state including modification times, permissions, and file hashes which can then be used to compare against the current state of the filesystem to detect modifications to the system. The audit requires the aide package (dpkg-query). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.1 Ensure AIDE is installed

audit.command:
command -v dpkg-query >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1

for p in aide; do s=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$p" 2>/dev/null); case "$s" in *' installed') ;; *) echo "$p is not installed"; bad=1 ;; esac; done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Install AIDE using the appropriate package manager or manual installation: # apt install aide aide-common Configure AIDE as appropriate for your environment. Consult the AIDE documentation for options. Initialize AIDE: # aideinit

title: Ensure filesystem integrity is regularly checked
description: Periodic checking of the filesystem integrity is needed to detect changes to the filesystem. The audit requires an enabled and active aidecheck.timer or a cron job (root crontab, /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.*) that runs aide. reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.2 Ensure filesystem integrity is regularly checked

e=$(systemctl is-enabled aidecheck.timer 2>/dev/null)
[ "$e" = enabled ] && systemctl is-active --quiet aidecheck.timer && { echo compliant; exit 0; }
c=$( (crontab -u root -l 2>/dev/null; cat /etc/crontab /etc/cron.d/* 2>/dev/null; ls /etc/cron.daily /etc/cron.weekly 2>/dev/null) | grep -E '(^|[^#].*)\baide' )
[ -n "$c" ] && echo compliant || echo 'no aidecheck.timer or aide cron job'

remediation.command: Run the following commands: # cp ./config/aidecheck.service /etc/systemd/system/aidecheck.service # cp ./config/aidecheck.timer /etc/systemd/system/aidecheck.timer # chmod 0644 /etc/systemd/system/aidecheck.* # systemctl reenable aidecheck.timer # systemctl restart aidecheck.timer # systemctl daemon-reload OR Run the following command: # crontab -u root -e Add the following line to the crontab: 0 5 * * * /usr/bin/aide.wrapper --config /etc/aide/aide.conf --check

title: Ensure permissions on bootloader config are configured
description: The grub configuration file contains information on boot settings and passwords for unlocking boot options. The grub configuration is usually grub.cfg stored in /boot/grub/. title: Ensure bootloader password is set

reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.2 Ensure bootloader password is set

title: Ensure authentication required for single user mode
description: Single user mode is used for recovery when the system detects an issue during boot or by manual selection from the bootloader. The audit requires the root account to have a password set in /etc/shadow, so single-user mode asks for it. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.3 Ensure authentication required for single user mode

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
grep -Eq '^root:[*!]:' /etc/shadow && echo 'root has no password (single-user mode unprotected)' || echo compliant

remediation.command: Run the following command and follow the prompts to set a password for the root user: # passwd root

title: Ensure interactive boot is not enabled
description: Interactive boot allows console users to interactively select which services start on boot. Not all distributions support this capability. The PROMPT_FOR_CONFIRM option provides console users the ability to interactively boot the system and select which services to start on boot . Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5.4 Ensure interactive boot is not enabled

audit.command: If interactive boot is available verify it is disabled on your system. On some distributions this is configured via the PROMPT_FOR_CONFIRM option in /etc/sysconfig/boot : # grep "^PROMPT_FOR_CONFIRM=" /etc/sysconfig/boot PROMPT_FOR_CONFIRM="no"

remediation.command: If interactive boot is available disable it.

title: Ensure XD/NX support is enabled
description: Recent processors in the x86 family support the ability to prevent code execution on a per memory page basis. Generically and on AMD processors, this ability is called No Execute (NX), while on Intel processors it is called Execute Disable (XD). This ability can help prevent exploitation of buffer overflow vulnerabilities and should be activated whenever possible. The audit requires the nx CPU flag (or the kernel "NX (Execute Disable) protection: active" message) and no noexec=off on the kernel command line. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.1 Ensure XD/NX support is enabled

audit.command:
grep -Eq 'noexec[0-9]*=off' /proc/cmdline && { echo 'NX disabled on the kernel command line'; exit 1; }
grep -Eqw 'nx' /proc/cpuinfo && echo compliant || { journalctl -k 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'protection: active' && echo compliant || echo 'NX/XD protection not active'; }

remediation.command: On 32 bit systems install a kernel with PAE support, no installation is required on 64 bit systems: If necessary configure your bootloader to load the new kernel and reboot the system. You may need to enable NX or XD support in your bios.

title: Ensure address space layout randomization (ASLR) is enabled
description: Address space layout randomization (ASLR) is an exploit mitigation technique which randomly arranges the address space of key data areas of a process. The audit requires the running value and the persisted sysctl setting to be 2. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.2 Ensure address space layout randomization (ASLR) is enabled

remediation.guidance: Set the following parameter in /etc/sysctl.conf or a /etc/sysctl.d/* file: kernel.randomize_va_space = 2 Run the following command to set the active kernel parameter: # sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=2

title: Ensure prelink is disabled
description: prelink is a program that modifies ELF shared libraries and ELF dynamically linked binaries in such a way that the time needed for the dynamic linker to perform relocations at startup significantly decreases. The audit requires the prelink package not to be installed. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.3 Ensure prelink is disabled

bad=0
for p in prelink; do
  s=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$p" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$s" in *' installed') echo "$p is installed"; bad=1 ;; esac
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to restore binaries to normal: # prelink -ua Uninstall prelink using the appropriate package manager or manual installation: # apt purge prelink

title: Ensure core dumps are restricted

The system provides the ability to set a soft limit for core dumps, but this can be overridden by the user. The audit requires "* hard core 0" in limits.conf (or limits.d) and fs.suid_dumpable = 0 running and persisted. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6.4 Ensure core dumps are restricted

remediation.command: Add the following line to /etc/security/limits.conf or a /etc/security/limits.d/* file: * hard core 0 Set the following parameter in /etc/sysctl.conf or a /etc/sysctl.d/* file: fs.suid_dumpable = 0 Run the following command to set the active kernel parameter: # sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=0 If systemd-coredump is installed: edit /etc/systemd/coredump.conf and add/modify the following lines: Storage=none ProcessSizeMax=0 Run the command: systemctl daemon-reload

title: Ensure AppArmor is installed
description: AppArmor provides Mandatory Access Controls. The audit requires the apparmor and apparmor-utils packages. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.

bad=0

[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

title: Ensure AppArmor is enabled in the bootloader configuration
description: Configure AppArmor to be enabled at boot time and verify that it has not been overwritten by the bootloader boot parameters. The audit requires apparmor=1 and security=apparmor on every linux line of /boot/grub/grub.cfg. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.2 Ensure AppArmor is enabled in the bootloader configuration

audit.command:
f=/boot/grub/grub.cfg; [ -r "$f" ] || f=/boot/grub2/grub.cfg; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
l=$(grep -E '^\s*linux' "$f" | grep -v '/boot/memtest86+')
[ -n "$l" ] || { echo 'no linux lines in grub.cfg'; exit 1; }
bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$l" | grep -Ev '(\s)apparmor=1(\s|$)')
[ -z "$bad" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$l" | grep -Ev '(\s)security=apparmor(\s|$)' | grep -q . && echo 'kernel lines without security=apparmor' || echo compliant; } || echo 'kernel lines without apparmor=1'

title: Ensure all AppArmor Profiles are in enforce or complain mode
description: AppArmor profiles define what resources applications are able to access. The audit runs apparmor_status and requires loaded profiles (enforce or complain) and no unconfined processes that have a profile. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.3 Ensure all AppArmor Profiles are in enforce or complain mode

out=$(apparmor_status 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
l=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/profiles are loaded/{print $1; exit}')
u=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/processes are unconfined/{print $1; exit}')
[ "${l:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo 'no AppArmor profiles loaded'; exit 1; }
[ "${u:-0}" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "$u processes are unconfined"

remediation.command: Run the following command to set all profiles to enforce mode: # aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/* OR Run the following command to set all profiles to complain mode: # aa-complain /etc/apparmor.d/* Any unconfined processes may need to have a profile created or activated for them and then be restarted.

title: Ensure all AppArmor Profiles are enforcing
description: AppArmor profiles define what resources applications are able to access. The audit runs apparmor_status and requires every loaded profile to be in enforce mode and no unconfined processes. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7.1.4 Ensure all AppArmor Profiles are enforcing

audit.command:
out=$(apparmor_status 2>/dev/null) || exit 1

u=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/processes are unconfined/{print $1; exit}')
[ "${l:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { echo 'no AppArmor profiles loaded'; exit 1; }
[ "${c:-0}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${u:-0}" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "complain: ${c:-0}, unconfined: ${u:-0}"

description: System time should be synchronized between all systems in an environment. The audit requires systemd-timesyncd enabled or the chrony or ntp package installed (host-based VM time sync must be verified manually). [ "$s" = enabled ] && { echo compliant; exit 0; }

for p in chrony ntp; do s=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$p" 2>/dev/null); case "$s" in *' installed') echo compliant; exit 0 ;; esac; done

In contrast to NTP implementations such as chrony or the NTP reference server this only implements a client side, and does not bother with the full NTP complexity, focusing only on querying time from one remote server and synchronizing the ... title: Ensure nftables rules are permanent
description: nftables is a subsystem of the Linux kernel providing filtering and classification of network packets/datagrams/frames. The nftables service reads the /etc/sysconfig/nftables.conf file for a nftables file or files to include in the nftables ruleset. A nftables ruleset containing the input, forward, and output base chains allow network traffic to be filtered. Applies when nftables is installed: the audit requires /etc/nftables.conf (and the files it includes) to define the input, forward and output base chains so they load at boot. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.3.8 Ensure nftables rules are permanent

audit.command:
f=/etc/nftables.conf; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
inc=$(awk '$1 ~ /^\s*include/ { gsub("\"","",$2); print $2 }' "$f")
all=$(cat "$f" $inc 2>/dev/null)
bad=0; for h in input forward output; do printf '%s\n' "$all" | grep -q "hook $h" || { echo "hook $h not in the boot ruleset"; bad=1; }; done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/sysconfig/nftables.conf file and un-comment or add a line with include <Absolute path to nftables rules file> for each nftables file you want included in the nftables ruleset on boot example: # vi /etc/sysconfig/nftables.conf Add the line: include "/etc/nftables/nftables.rules"

title: Ensure default deny firewall policy
description: A default deny all policy on connections ensures that any unconfigured network usage will be rejected. Applies when iptables rules are persisted (/etc/iptables/rules.v4): the audit requires DROP or REJECT policies on INPUT, FORWARD and OUTPUT. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4.4.1.1 Ensure default deny firewall policy

audit.command:
out=$(iptables -L -n 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=0
for c in INPUT FORWARD OUTPUT; do
  p=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n "s/^Chain $c (policy \([A-Z]*\).*/\1/p")
  case "$p" in DROP|REJECT) ;; *) echo "$c policy ${p:-unknown}"; bad=1 ;; esac
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to implement a default DROP policy: # iptables -P INPUT DROP # iptables -P OUTPUT DROP # iptables -P FORWARD DROP

title: Ensure login and logout events are collected
description: Monitor login and logout events. The parameters below track changes to files associated with login/logout events. The file /var/log/faillog tracks failed events from login. The file /var/log/lastlog maintain records of the last time a user successfully logged in. The file /var/log/tallylog maintains records of failures via the pam_tally2 module The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.7 Ensure login and logout events are collected

remediation.command: Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/logins.rules and add the following lines: -w /var/log/faillog -p wa -k logins -w /var/log/lastlog -p wa -k logins -w /var/log/tallylog -p wa -k logins

title: Ensure session initiation information is collected
description: Monitor session initiation events. The parameters in this section track changes to the files associated with session events. The file /var/run/utmp tracks all currently logged in users. All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "session." The /var/log/wtmp file tracks logins, logouts, shutdown, and reboot events. The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.8 Ensure session initiation information is collected

remediation.command: Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/session.rules and add the following lines: -w /var/run/utmp -p wa -k session -w /var/log/wtmp -p wa -k logins -w /var/log/btmp -p wa -k logins

title: Ensure discretionary access control permission modification events are collected
description: Monitor changes to file permissions, attributes, ownership and group. The parameters in this section track changes for system calls that affect file permissions and attributes. The chmod , fchmod and fchmodat system calls affect the permissions associated with a file. The chown , fchown , fchownat and lchown system calls affect owner and group attributes on a file. The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l, 64-bit syscalls). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.9 Ensure discretionary access control permission modification events are collected

remediation.command: For 32 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/perm_mod.rules and add the following lines: -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -S lchown -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S fsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -S fremovexattr -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k perm_mod For 64 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/perm_mod.rules and add the ...

title: Ensure use of privileged commands is collected
description: Monitor privileged programs (those that have the setuid and/or setgid bit set on execution) to determine if unprivileged users are running these commands. Note: Systems may have been customized to change the default UID_MIN. The audit finds SUID/SGID programs on local filesystems and requires a loaded "-F path=<program> -F perm=x ... -k privileged" rule for each (auditctl -l). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.10 Ensure use of privileged commands is collected

audit.command:
command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(auditctl -l 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
files=$(findmnt -rn -l -o TARGET,FSTYPE | awk '$2 ~ /^(ext[234]|xfs|btrfs|zfs)$/ {print $1}' | while read -r m; do find "$m" -xdev \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -type f 2>/dev/null; done | sort -u)
bad=$(for f in $files; do printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Fq -- "path=$f " || echo "$f"; done)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || { echo 'privileged programs without an audit rule:'; printf '%s\n' "$bad" | head -n 20; }

remediation.command: To remediate this issue, the system administrator will have to execute a find command to locate all the privileged programs and then add an audit line for each one of them. The audit parameters associated with this are as follows: -F path=" $1 " - will populate each file name found through the find command and processed by awk. -F perm=x - will write an audit record if the file is executed. -F auid>=1000 - will write a record if the user executing the command is not a privileged user. -F auid!= 4294967295 - will ignore Daemon events All audit records should be tagged with the identifier "privileged".

title: Ensure successful file system mounts are collected
description: Monitor the use of the mount system call. The mount (and umount ) system call controls the mounting and unmounting of file systems. The parameters below configure the system to create an audit record when the mount system call is used by a non-privileged user Note: Systems may have been customized to change the default UID_MIN. The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l, 64-bit syscalls). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.11 Ensure successful file system mounts are collected

audit.command:
command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(auditctl -l 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=0
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '(-k |key=)mounts( |$)' | grep -F 'arch=b64' | grep -Eq -- '-S ([^ ]*,)?mount(,| |$)' || { echo 'missing b64 syscall rule: mount -k mounts'; bad=1; }
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: For 32 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/audit.rules and add the following lines: -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S mount -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts For 64 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/mounts.rules and add the following lines: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S mount -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S mount -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=4294967295 -k mounts

title: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected
description: Monitor scope changes for system administrations. If the system has been properly configured to force system administrators to log in as themselves first and then use the sudo command to execute privileged commands, it is possible to monitor changes in scope. The file /etc/sudoers will be written to when the file or its attributes have changed. The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.12 Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected

remediation.command: Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/scope.rules and add the following lines: -w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope -w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k scope

title: Ensure system administrator actions (sudolog) are collected
description: Monitor the sudo log file. If the system has been properly configured to disable the use of the su command and force all administrators to have to log in first and then use sudo to execute privileged commands, then all administrator commands will be logged to /var/log/sudo.log . The audit reads the sudo logfile from sudoers and requires a loaded "-w <logfile> -p wa -k actions" rule (auditctl -l). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.13 Ensure system administrator actions (sudolog) are collected

audit.command:
command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(auditctl -l 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
l=$(grep -rhs 'logfile=' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d | sed -e 's/.*logfile=//;s/,\? .*//' | tr -d '"' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$l" ] || { echo 'sudo logfile is not configured'; exit 1; }
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '(-k |key=)actions( |$)' | grep -Fq -- "-w $l " && echo compliant || echo "missing watch: -w $l -p wa -k actions"

remediation.command: Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules and add the following line: -w <Path to sudo logfile> -p wa -k actions Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/actions.rules and add the following line: -w /var/log/sudo.log -p wa -k actions

title: Ensure kernel module loading and unloading is collected
description: Monitor the loading and unloading of kernel modules. The programs insmod (install a kernel module), rmmod (remove a kernel module), and modprobe (a more sophisticated program to load and unload modules, as well as some other features) control loading and unloading of modules. The audit inspects the loaded rules (auditctl -l, 64-bit syscalls). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.14 Ensure kernel module loading and unloading is collected

remediation.command: For 32 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/modules.rules and add the following lines: -w /sbin/insmod -p x -k modules -w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k modules -w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k modules -a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S init_module -S delete_module -k modules For 64 bit systems Edit or create a file in the /etc/audit/rules.d/ directory ending in .rules Example: vi /etc/audit/rules.d/modules.rules and add the following lines: -w /sbin/insmod -p x -k modules -w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k modules -w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k modules -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S init_module -S delete_module -k modules

title: Ensure the audit configuration is immutable
description: Set system audit so that audit rules cannot be modified with auditctl . Setting the flag "-e 2" forces audit to be put in immutable mode. Audit changes can only be made on system reboot. The audit requires "-e 2" as the last rule in /etc/audit/audit.rules. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.15 Ensure the audit configuration is immutable

audit.command:
f=/etc/audit/audit.rules; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
l=$(grep '^\s*[^#]' "$f" | tail -n 1 | tr -s ' ')
[ "$l" = '-e 2' ] && echo compliant || echo "last audit rule: ${l:-none}"

remediation.guidance: Edit or create the file /etc/audit/rules.d/99-finalize.rules and add the line -e 2 at the end of the file

title: Ensure rsyslog is installed
description: The rsyslog software is a recommended replacement to the original syslogd daemon which provide improvements over syslogd, such as connection-oriented (i.e. TCP) transmission of logs, the option to log to database formats, and the encryption of log data en route to a central logging server. The audit requires rsyslog (or syslog-ng) to be installed. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.1 Ensure rsyslog is installed

audit.command:
command -v dpkg-query >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
for p in rsyslog syslog-ng; do s=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$p" 2>/dev/null); case "$s" in *' installed') echo compliant; exit 0 ;; esac; done
echo 'none of rsyslog syslog-ng is installed'

remediation.guidance: Install rsyslog: # apt install rsyslog

title: Ensure rsyslog Service is enabled
description: Once the rsyslog package is installed it needs to be activated. The audit requires the rsyslog service to be enabled. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.2 Ensure rsyslog Service is enabled

audit.command:
command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
s=$(systemctl is-enabled rsyslog 2>/dev/null)
[ "$s" = enabled ] && echo compliant || echo "rsyslog: ${s:-not found}"

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to enable rsyslog: # systemctl --now enable rsyslog

title: Ensure logging is configured
description: The /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf files specifies rules for logging and which files are to be used to log certain classes of messages. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.3 Ensure logging is configured

audit.command: Review the contents of the /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf files to ensure appropriate logging is set. In addition, run the following command and verify that the log files are logging information: # ls -l /var/log/

remediation.command: Edit the following lines in the /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf files as appropriate for your environment: *.emerg :omusrmsg:* auth,authpriv.* /var/log/auth.log mail.* -/var/log/mail mail.info -/var/log/mail.info mail.warning -/var/log/mail.warn mail.err /var/log/mail.err news.crit -/var/log/news/news.crit news.err -/var/log/news/news.err news.notice -/var/log/news/news.notice *.=warning;*.=err -/var/log/warn *.crit /var/log/warn *.*;mail.none;news.none -/var/log/messages local0,local1.* -/var/log/localmessages local2,local3.* -/var/log/localmessages local4,local5.* -/var/log/localmessages local6,local7.* -/var/log/localmessages Run the following command to reload the rsyslog ...

title: Ensure rsyslog default file permissions configured
description: rsyslog will create logfiles that do not already exist on the system. This setting controls what permissions will be applied to these newly created files. The audit requires $FileCreateMode 0640 or more restrictive in /etc/rsyslog.conf or rsyslog.d. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.4 Ensure rsyslog default file permissions configured

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf files and set $FileCreateMode to 0640 or more restrictive: $FileCreateMode 0640

title: Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host
description: The rsyslog utility supports the ability to send logs it gathers to a remote log host running syslogd(8) or to receive messages from remote hosts, reducing administrative overhead. The audit requires an rsyslog action with target= or a *.* @host forwarding rule. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.5 Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host

audit.command:
grep -Ehs '^[^#]*action\(' /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf | grep -q 'target=' && { echo compliant; exit 0; }
grep -Ehs '^[^#]\s*\S+\.\*\s+@' /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf | grep -q . && echo compliant || echo 'no remote log host configured'

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf files and add one of the following lines: Newer syntax: <files to sent to the remote log server> action(type="omfwd" target="<FQDN or ip of loghost>" port="<port number>" protocol="tcp" action.resumeRetryCount="<number of re-tries>" queue.type="linkList" queue.size=<number of messages to queue>") Example: *.* action(type="omfwd" target="192.168.2.100" port"514" protocol="tcp" action.resumeRetryCount="100" queue.type="linkList" queue.size="1000") Older syntax: *.* @@<FQDN or ip of loghost> Example: *.* @@192.168.2.100 Run the following command to reload the rsyslog configuration: # systemctl reload rsyslog

title: Ensure remote rsyslog messages are only accepted on designated log hosts.
description: By default, rsyslog does not listen for log messages coming in from remote systems. The ModLoad tells rsyslog to load the imtcp.so module so it can listen over a network via TCP. The InputTCPServerRun option instructs rsyslogd to listen on the specified TCP port. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.1.6 Ensure remote rsyslog messages are only accepted on designated log hosts.

audit.command: Run the following commands and verify the resulting lines are uncommented on designated log hosts and commented or removed on all others: # grep '$ModLoad imtcp' /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf $ModLoad imtcp # grep '$InputTCPServerRun' /etc/rsyslog.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf $InputTCPServerRun 514

remediation.command: For hosts that are designated as log hosts, edit the /etc/rsyslog.conf file and un- comment or add the following lines: $ModLoad imtcp $InputTCPServerRun 514 For hosts that are not designated as log hosts, edit the /etc/rsyslog.conf file and comment or remove the following lines: # $ModLoad imtcp # $InputTCPServerRun 514 Run the following command to reload the rsyslogd configuration: # systemctl restart rsyslog

title: Ensure journald is configured to send logs to rsyslog
description: Data from journald may be stored in volatile memory or persisted locally on the server. Utilities exist to accept remote export of journald logs, however, use of the rsyslog service provides a consistent means of log collection and export. The audit requires ForwardToSyslog=yes in journald.conf. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.2.1 Ensure journald is configured to send logs to rsyslog

audit.command: grep -Pqs -- '^\s*ForwardToSyslog\s*=\s*yes\b' /etc/systemd/journald.conf /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf && echo compliant || echo 'ForwardToSyslog=yes is not set'

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/systemd/journald.conf file and add the following line: ForwardToSyslog=yes

title: Ensure journald is configured to compress large log files
description: The journald system includes the capability of compressing overly large files to avoid filling up the system with logs or making the logs unmanageably large. The audit requires Compress=yes in journald.conf. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.2.2 Ensure journald is configured to compress large log files

audit.command: grep -Pqs -- '^\s*Compress\s*=\s*yes\b' /etc/systemd/journald.conf /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf && echo compliant || echo 'Compress=yes is not set'

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/systemd/journald.conf file and add the following line: Compress=yes

title: Ensure journald is configured to write logfiles to persistent disk
description: Data from journald may be stored in volatile memory or persisted locally on the server. Logs in memory will be lost upon a system reboot. By persisting logs to local disk on the server they are protected from loss. The audit requires Storage=persistent in journald.conf. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.2.3 Ensure journald is configured to write logfiles to persistent disk

audit.command: grep -Pqs -- '^\s*Storage\s*=\s*persistent\b' /etc/systemd/journald.conf /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf && echo compliant || echo 'Storage=persistent is not set'

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/systemd/journald.conf file and add the following line: Storage=persistent

title: Ensure permissions on all logfiles are configured
description: Log files stored in /var/log/ contain logged information from many services on the system, or on log hosts others as well. The audit requires no file under /var/log with group write/execute or any other permission. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2.3 Ensure permissions on all logfiles are configured

remediation.guidance: Run the following commands to set permissions on all existing log files: find /var/log -type f -exec chmod g-wx,o-rwx "{}" + -o -type d -exec chmod g- w,o-rwx "{}" +

title: Ensure logrotate is configured
description: The system includes the capability of rotating log files regularly to avoid filling up the system with logs or making the logs unmanageably large. The file /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog is the configuration file used to rotate log files created by rsyslog. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure logrotate is configured

audit.command: Review /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog and verify logs are rotated according to site policy.

remediation.command: Edit /etc/logrotate.conf and /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog to ensure logs are rotated according to site policy.

title: Ensure cron daemon is enabled
description: The cron daemon is used to execute batch jobs on the system. The audit requires the cron service to be enabled. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure cron daemon is enabled

audit.command:
command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
s=$(systemctl is-enabled cron 2>/dev/null)
[ "$s" = enabled ] && echo compliant || echo "cron: ${s:-not found}"

remediation.guidance: Based on your system configuration, run the appropriate one of the following commands to enable cron: # systemctl --now enable cron

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/crontab are configured
description: The /etc/crontab file is used by cron to control its own jobs. The commands in this item make sure that root is the user and group owner of the file and that only the owner can access the file. The audit requires /etc/crontab root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.2 Ensure permissions on /etc/crontab are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/crontab : # chown root:root /etc/crontab # chmod og-rwx /etc/crontab

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.hourly are configured
description: This directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on an hourly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory. The audit requires /etc/cron.hourly root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.hourly are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/cron.hourly : # chown root:root /etc/cron.hourly # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.hourly

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.daily are configured
description: The /etc/cron.daily directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a daily basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory. The audit requires /etc/cron.daily root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.4 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.daily are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/cron.daily : # chown root:root /etc/cron.daily # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.daily

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.weekly are configured
description: The /etc/cron.weekly directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a weekly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory. The audit requires /etc/cron.weekly root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.5 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.weekly are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/cron.weekly : # chown root:root /etc/cron.weekly # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.weekly

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.monthly are configured
description: The /etc/cron.monthly directory contains system cron jobs that need to run on a monthly basis. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The commands below restrict read/write and search access to user and group root, preventing regular users from accessing this directory. The audit requires /etc/cron.monthly root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.6 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.monthly are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/cron.monthly : # chown root:root /etc/cron.monthly # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.monthly

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.d are configured
description: The /etc/cron.d directory contains system cron jobs that need to run in a similar manner to the hourly, daily weekly and monthly jobs from /etc/crontab , but require more granular control as to when they run. The files in this directory cannot be manipulated by the crontab command, but are instead edited by system administrators using a text editor. The audit requires /etc/cron.d root:root with no group/other permissions. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.7 Ensure permissions on /etc/cron.d are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set ownership and permissions on /etc/cron.d : # chown root:root /etc/cron.d # chmod og-rwx /etc/cron.d

title: Ensure at/cron is restricted to authorized users
description: Configure /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow to allow specific users to use these services. If /etc/cron.allow or /etc/at.allow do not exist, then /etc/at.deny and /etc/cron.deny are checked. Any user not specifically defined in those files is allowed to use at and cron. By removing the files, only users in /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow are allowed to use at and cron. The audit requires /etc/cron.deny and /etc/at.deny to be absent and /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow root:root with no group write/execute and no other permissions. out=$(sshd -T -C user=root -C host="$(hostname)" -C addr="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)" 2>/dev/null) || out=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'tolower($1)=="maxsessions"{print $2; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "MaxSessions ${v:-unset}"; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$v" -le 4 ] && [ "$v" -ge 1 ] && echo compliant || echo "MaxSessions $v"

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter as follows: MaxSessions 4

title: Ensure password creation requirements are configured
description: The pam_pwquality.so module checks the strength of passwords. It performs checks such as making sure a password is not a dictionary word, it is a certain length, contains a mix of characters (e.g. alphabet, numeric, other) and more. The following are definitions of the pam_pwquality.so options. The audit requires minlen 14 or more, minclass 4 (or dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit = -1) in pwquality.conf and pam_pwquality.so retry=1-3 in /etc/pam.d/common-password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure password creation requirements are configured

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to install the pam_pwquality module: apt install libpam-pwquality Edit the file /etc/security/pwquality.conf and add or modify the following line for password length to conform to site policy minlen = 14 Edit the file /etc/security/pwquality.conf and add or modify the following line for password complexity to conform to site policy minclass = 4 OR dcredit = -1 ucredit = -1 ocredit = -1 lcredit = -1 Edit the /etc/pam.d/common-password file to include the appropriate options for pam_pwquality.so and to conform to site policy: password requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3

title: Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured
description: Lock out users after n unsuccessful consecutive login attempts. The first sets of changes are made to the PAM configuration files. The second set of changes are applied to the program specific PAM configuration file. The second set of changes must be applied to each program that will lock out users. The audit requires pam_tally2.so with deny=5 or less in common-auth and pam_deny.so plus pam_tally2.so in common-account (the benchmark example also sets unlock_time=900). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.2 Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/pam.d/common-auth file and add the auth line below: auth required pam_tally2.so onerr=fail audit silent deny=5 unlock_time=900 Edit the /etc/pam.d/common-account file and add the account lines bellow: account requisite pam_deny.so account required pam_tally.so Note: If a user has been locked out because they have reached the maximum consecutive failure count defined by deny= in the pam_tally2.so module, the user can be unlocked by issuing the command /sbin/pam_tally2 -u <username> --reset. This command sets the failed count to 0, effectively unlocking the user.

title: Ensure password reuse is limited
description: The /etc/security/opasswd file stores the users' old passwords and can be checked to ensure that users are not recycling recent passwords. The audit requires pam_pwhistory.so with remember=5 or more in /etc/pam.d/common-password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.3 Ensure password reuse is limited

remediation.command: Edit the /etc/pam.d/common-password file to include the remember option and conform to site policy as shown: password required pam_pwhistory.so remember=5

title: Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512
description: The commands below change password encryption from md5 to sha512 (a much stronger hashing algorithm). All existing accounts will need to perform a password change to upgrade the stored hashes to the new algorithm. The audit requires the pam_unix.so password line in /etc/pam.d/common-password to include sha512. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.4 Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512

audit.command: grep -Pqs -- '^\s*password\s+(\S+\s+)+pam_unix\.so\s+(\S+\s+)*sha512\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password && echo compliant || echo 'pam_unix.so does not use sha512'

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/pam.d/common-password file to include the sha512 option for pam_unix.so as shown: password [success=1 default=ignore] pam_unix.so sha512

title: Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less
description: The PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to force passwords to expire once they reach a defined age. It is recommended that the PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter be set to less than or equal to 365 days. The audit requires PASS_MAX_DAYS 365 or less in /etc/login.defs and for every user with a password in /etc/shadow. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.1 Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
d=$(awk '$1 == "PASS_MAX_DAYS" {print $2}' /etc/login.defs)
case "$d" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'PASS_MAX_DAYS not set'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$d" -le 365 ] || { echo 'PASS_MAX_DAYS '"$d"; exit 1; }
bad=$(awk -F: '($2 !~ /^[!*]/ && $2 != "") { v = $5; if (v == "" || !(v + 0 <= 365)) print $1 ": " (v == "" ? "unset" : v) }' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$bad"

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter to conform to site policy in /etc/login.defs : PASS_MAX_DAYS 365 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --maxdays 365 <user>

title: Ensure minimum days between password changes is configured
description: The PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to prevent users from changing their password until a minimum number of days have passed since the last time the user changed their password. It is recommended that PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter be set to 1 or more days. The audit requires PASS_MIN_DAYS 1 or more in /etc/login.defs and for every user with a password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.2 Ensure minimum days between password changes is configured

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
d=$(awk '$1 == "PASS_MIN_DAYS" {print $2}' /etc/login.defs)
case "$d" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'PASS_MIN_DAYS not set'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$d" -ge 1 ] || { echo 'PASS_MIN_DAYS '"$d"; exit 1; }
bad=$(awk -F: '($2 !~ /^[!*]/ && $2 != "") { v = $4; if (v == "" || !(v + 0 >= 1)) print $1 ": " (v == "" ? "unset" : v) }' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$bad"

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter to 1 in /etc/login.defs : PASS_MIN_DAYS 1 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --mindays 1 <user>

title: Ensure password expiration warning days is 7 or more
description: The PASS_WARN_AGE parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to notify users that their password will expire in a defined number of days. It is recommended that the PASS_WARN_AGE parameter be set to 7 or more days. The audit requires PASS_WARN_AGE 7 or more in /etc/login.defs and for every user with a password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.3 Ensure password expiration warning days is 7 or more

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
d=$(awk '$1 == "PASS_WARN_AGE" {print $2}' /etc/login.defs)
case "$d" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'PASS_WARN_AGE not set'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$d" -ge 7 ] || { echo 'PASS_WARN_AGE '"$d"; exit 1; }
bad=$(awk -F: '($2 !~ /^[!*]/ && $2 != "") { v = $6; if (v == "" || !(v + 0 >= 7)) print $1 ": " (v == "" ? "unset" : v) }' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$bad"

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_WARN_AGE parameter to 7 in /etc/login.defs : PASS_WARN_AGE 7 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --warndays 7 <user>

title: Ensure inactive password lock is 30 days or less
description: User accounts that have been inactive for over a given period of time can be automatically disabled. It is recommended that accounts that are inactive for 30 days after password expiration be disabled. The audit requires useradd -D INACTIVE of 30 days or less and an inactivity value of 30 or less for every user with a password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.4 Ensure inactive password lock is 30 days or less

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
d=$(useradd -D 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^INACTIVE=//p')
case "$d" in ''|-*|*[!0-9]*) echo "useradd INACTIVE=${d:-unset}"; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$d" -le 30 ] || { echo "useradd INACTIVE=$d"; exit 1; }
bad=$(awk -F: '($2 !~ /^[!*]/ && $2 != "") { v = $7; if (v == "" || v + 0 > 30 || v + 0 < 0) print $1 ": " (v == "" ? "unset" : v) }' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$bad"

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the default password inactivity period to 30 days: # useradd -D -f 30 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --inactive 30 <user>

title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past. The audit requires every last password change date in /etc/shadow to be in the past. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1.5 Ensure all users last password change date is in the past

audit.command:
[ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1
today=$(( $(date +%s) / 86400 ))
bad=$(awk -F: -v t="$today" '($3 != "" && $3 + 0 > t) {print $1}' /etc/shadow)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || echo "future password change date: $(printf '%s ' $bad)"

remediation.guidance: Investigate any users with a password change date in the future and correct them. Locking the account, expiring the password, or resetting the password manually may be appropriate.

title: Ensure system accounts are secured
description: There are a number of accounts provided with most distributions that are used to manage applications and are not intended to provide an interactive shell. The audit requires system accounts (UID below UID_MIN, except root/sync/shutdown/halt) to have a nologin/false shell and a locked password. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.2 Ensure system accounts are secured

remediation.guidance: Run the commands appropriate for your distribution: Set the shell for any accounts returned by the audit to nologin: # usermod -s $(which nologin) <user> Lock any non root accounts returned by the audit: # usermod -L <user> The following command will set all system accounts to a non login shell: awk -F: '($1!="root" && $1!="sync" && $1!="shutdown" && $1!="halt" && $1!~/^\+/ && $3<'"$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)"' && $7!="'"$(which nologin)"'" && $7!="/bin/false") {print $1}' /etc/passwd | while read -r user; do usermod -s "$(which nologin)" "$user"

title: Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0
description: The usermod command can be used to specify which group the root user belongs to. This affects permissions of files that are created by the root user. The audit requires the root account primary group to be GID 0. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.3 Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0

audit.command:
g=$(awk -F: '$1 == "root" {print $4}' /etc/passwd) || exit 1
[ "$g" = 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "root primary GID: $g"

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the root user default group to GID 0 : # usermod -g 0 root

title: Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive
description: The default umask determines the permissions of files created by users. The user creating the file has the discretion of making their files and directories readable by others via the chmod command. Users who wish to allow their files and directories to be readable by others by default may choose a different default umask by inserting the umask command into the standard shell ... The audit requires every umask in /etc/bash.bashrc, /etc/profile and /etc/profile.d/*.sh to be 027 or more restrictive (and at least one to exist). Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.4 Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive

audit.command:
files="/etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bashrc /etc/profile $(ls /etc/profile.d/*.sh 2>/dev/null)"
found=0; bad=0
for f in $files; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  for u in $(grep -Ehoi '^[^#]*\bumask[[:space:]]+[0-7]{3,4}' "$f" | grep -Eo '[0-7]{3,4}$'); do
    found=1; [ $(( 8#$u & 027 )) -eq $(( 8#027 )) ] || { echo "$f: umask $u"; bad=1; }
  done
done
[ "$found" -eq 1 ] || { echo 'no umask setting found'; exit 1; }
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/bash.bashrc, /etc/profile and /etc/profile.d/*.sh files (and the appropriate files for any other shell supported on your system) and add or edit any umask parameters as follows: umask 027

title: Ensure default user shell timeout is 900 seconds or less
description: The default TMOUT determines the shell timeout for users. The TMOUT value is measured in seconds. The audit requires TMOUT between 1 and 900 in the shell startup files and no larger TMOUT value. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.5 Ensure default user shell timeout is 900 seconds or less

audit.command:
ok=0; bad=0
for f in /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bashrc /etc/profile $(ls /etc/profile.d/*.sh 2>/dev/null); do [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  for v in $(grep -Ehoi '^[^#]*\bTMOUT=[0-9]+' "$f" | grep -Eo '[0-9]+$'); do
    if [ "$v" -ge 1 ] && [ "$v" -le 900 ]; then ok=1; else echo "$f: TMOUT=$v"; bad=1; fi
  done
done
[ "$ok" -eq 1 ] || { echo 'TMOUT (900 or less) is not set'; exit 1; }
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y remove "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_pkg_install() { for p in "$@"; do
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }
tma_svc_off() { for u in "$@"; do systemctl stop "$u" 2>/dev/null; systemctl mask "$u" 2>/dev/null; done; return 0; }
tma_ts=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$tma_ts"; }
tma_applied() { return 0; }

# make every umask line in the given files at least 027
tma_umask_fix() { for f in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  grep -Eqi '^[[:space:]]*umask[[:space:]]' "$f" || continue
  t=$(mktemp); ch=0
  while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
    if [[ $line =~ ^([[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+)0*([0-7]{1,4})([[:space:]#].*)?$ ]]; then
      v=$((8#${BASH_REMATCH[2]})); n=$((v | 8#027))
      if [ "$n" != "$v" ]; then line="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}$(printf '%03o' $n)${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"; ch=1; fi
    elif [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*[Uu][Mm][Aa][Ss][Kk][[:space:]]+[ugoa]*= ]] && [[ $line =~ (g=[rwx]*w|o=[rwx]*[rwx]) ]]; then
      line="umask 027"; ch=1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$t"
  done < "$f"
  if [ $ch = 1 ]; then tma_bak "$f"; cat "$t" > "$f"; fi
  rm -f "$t"
done; }
N=900
# one authoritative file; any other TMOUT assignment is commented out (audit demands readonly+export in each file mentioning it)
for f in /etc/profile /etc/bashrc /etc/bash.bashrc /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile.d/*.sh; do
  [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] || continue
  [ "$f" = /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh ] && continue
  grep -Eq '^[^#]*\bTMOUT\b' "$f" || continue
  tma_bak "$f"; sed -i -E '/^[[:space:]]*#/! s/^([^#]*\bTMOUT\b.*)$/# tmaegis: \1/' "$f"
done
mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
printf '# CIS: idle shell timeout\nTMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" > /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/50-tmaegis-tmout.sh
for f in /etc/bash/bashrc /etc/profile; do [ -f "$f" ] && ! grep -q '^TMOUT=' "$f" && [ "$f" = /etc/bash/bashrc ] && printf 'TMOUT=%s\nreadonly TMOUT\nexport TMOUT\n' "$N" >> "$f"; done
true
remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/bashrc, /etc/profile and /etc/profile.d/*.sh files (and the appropriate files for any other shell supported on your system) and add or edit any TMOUT parameters in accordance with site policy: readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT Note: setting the value to readonly prevents unwanted modification during runtime.

title: Ensure root login is restricted to system console
description: The file /etc/securetty contains a list of valid terminals that may be logged in directly as root. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5 Ensure root login is restricted to system console

audit.command: # cat /etc/securetty

remediation.command: Remove entries for any consoles that are not in a physically secure location.

title: Ensure access to the su command is restricted
description: The su command allows a user to run a command or shell as another user. The program has been superseded by sudo , which allows for more granular control over privileged access. Normally, the su command can be executed by any user. By uncommenting the pam_wheel.so statement in /etc/pam.d/su , the su command will only allow users in a specific groups to execute su. The audit requires "auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=<group>" in /etc/pam.d/su and that group to have no members. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.6 Ensure access to the su command is restricted

audit.command:
l=$(grep -E '^\s*auth\s+required\s+pam_wheel\.so(\s.*)?\suse_uid(\s.*)?\sgroup=\S+' /etc/pam.d/su) || { echo 'pam_wheel.so use_uid group=<group> not set in /etc/pam.d/su'; exit 1; }
g=$(printf '%s\n' "$l" | grep -Eo 'group=\S+' | head -n 1 | cut -d= -f2)
m=$(awk -F: -v g="$g" '$1 == g {print $4}' /etc/group)
[ -z "$m" ] && echo compliant || echo "group $g has members: $m"

remediation.command: Create an empty group that will be specified for use of the su command. The group should be named according to site policy. groupadd sugroup Add the following line to the /etc/pam.d/su file, specifying the empty group: auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=sugroup

title: Audit system file permissions
description: The Ubuntu package manager has a number of useful options. One of these, the --verify option, can be used to verify that system packages are correctly installed. The --verify option can be used to verify a particular package or to verify all system packages. If no output is returned, the package is installed correctly. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.

audit.command: Run the following command to review all installed packages. Note that this may be very time consuming and may be best scheduled via the cron utility. It is recommended that the output of this command be redirected to a file that can be reviewed later. # dpkg --verify <package name>

remediation.command: Correct any discrepancies found and rerun the audit until output is clean or risk is mitigated or accepted.

title: Ensure permissions on /etc/gshadow are configured
description: The /etc/gshadow file is used to store the information about groups that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information. The audit requires /etc/gshadow owned by root, group root or shadow, mode 0640 or more restrictive. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.9 Ensure permissions on /etc/gshadow are configured

remediation.command: Run the following commands to set permissions on /etc/gshadow: # chown root:shadow /etc/gshadow # chmod o-rwx,g-wx /etc/gshadow

title: Ensure no world writable files exist
description: Unix-based systems support variable settings to control access to files. World writable files are the least secure. See the chmod(2) man page for more information. The audit searches local filesystems for world-writable files and requires none. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.10 Ensure no world writable files exist

audit.command:
command -v findmnt >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
mps=$(findmnt -rn -l -o TARGET,FSTYPE | awk '$2 !~ /^(nfs|nfs4|cifs|smb3|smbfs|fuse|proc|sysfs|tmpfs|devtmpfs|devpts|cgroup|cgroup2|pstore|securityfs|debugfs|tracefs|configfs|bpf|mqueue|hugetlbfs|autofs|binfmt_misc|efivarfs|overlay|squashfs|nsfs|ramfs|fusectl|rpc_pipefs)$/ {print $1}')
out=$(for m in $mps; do find "$m" -xdev -type f -perm -0002 -print 2>/dev/null; done | sort -u | head -n 50)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || { printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo 'world-writable files'; }

remediation.command: Removing write access for the "other" category ( chmod o-w <filename> ) is advisable, but always consult relevant vendor documentation to avoid breaking any application dependencies on a given file.
