title: Audit SUID executables
description: The owner of a file can set the file's permissions to run with the owner's or group's permissions, even if the user running the program is not the owner or a member of the group. The most common reason for a SUID program is to enable users to perform functions (such as changing their password) that require root privileges. Manual review against site policy. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.13 Audit SUID executables

audit.command: Run the following command to list SUID files: # df --local -P | awk '{if (NR!=1) print $6}' | xargs -I '{}' find '{}' -xdev -type f -perm -4000 The command above only searches local filesystems, there may still be compromised items on network mounted partitions. Additionally the --local option to df is not universal to all versions, it can be omitted to search all filesystems on a system including network mounted filesystems or the following command can be run manually for each partition: # find <partition> -xdev -type f -perm -4000

remediation.command: Ensure that no rogue SUID programs have been introduced into the system. Review the files returned by the action in the Audit section and confirm the integrity of these binaries.

title: Ensure all users' home directories exist
description: Users can be defined in /etc/passwd without a home directory or with a home directory that does not actually exist. The audit requires the home directory of every interactive user to exist. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.2 Ensure all users' home directories exist

audit.command:
users=$(awk -F: '($1 !~ /^(halt|sync|shutdown)$/ && $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/) {print $1":"$6}' /etc/passwd) || exit 1
bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$users" | while IFS=: read -r u d; do [ -d "$d" ] || echo "home directory $d of $u does not exist"; done)
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$bad"

remediation.guidance: If any users' home directories do not exist, create them and make sure the respective user owns the directory. Users without an assigned home directory should be removed or assigned a home directory as appropriate.

title: Ensure root PATH Integrity
description: The root user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the PATH is not set correctly. The audit checks root's PATH for empty entries, a trailing colon, '.', missing directories and directories not owned by root or group/world writable. Host-level control from the CIS ROS Melodic benchmark (Ubuntu 18.04 robot hosts); run as root.
reference: CIS ROS Melodic Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.4 Ensure root PATH Integrity

audit.command:
p=$(sudo -Hiu root env 2>/dev/null | grep '^PATH=' | cut -d= -f2-)
[ -n "$p" ] || p=$PATH
bad=0
case "$p" in *::*) echo 'empty directory in PATH (::)'; bad=1 ;; esac
case "$p" in *:) echo 'trailing : in PATH'; bad=1 ;; esac
IFS=:; for x in $p; do
  [ "$x" = . ] && { echo 'PATH contains .'; bad=1; continue; }
  if [ -d "$x" ]; then
    o=$(stat -Lc '%U' "$x"); m=$(stat -Lc '%a' "$x")
    [ "$o" = root ] || { echo "$x is not owned by root"; bad=1; }
    [ $(( 8#$m & 022 )) -eq 0 ] || { echo "$x is group or world writable"; bad=1; }
  else echo "$x is not a directory"; bad=1; fi
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Correct or justify any items discovered in the Audit step.

title: Ensure ROS 2 nodes use a dedicated, non-default DDS domain ID
description: All ROS 2 systems on a network share DDS domain 0 unless ROS_DOMAIN_ID is set, so unrelated robots and developer laptops cross-talk. A dedicated domain ID (0-101 on Linux) isolates the system; it is not an authentication control and complements SROS2. The audit inspects /proc/<pid>/environ of running processes containing ROS_DISTRO (run as root) and fails if none is found or any process has ROS_DOMAIN_ID unset or 0.
reference: CIS-style ROS 2 hardening guidance - DDS domain isolation (no CIS benchmark section; verify against your hardening standard)

audit.command:
found=0; bad=0
for e in /proc/[0-9]*/environ; do
  env=$( (tr '\0' '\n' < "$e") 2>/dev/null ) || continue
  case "$env" in *ROS_DISTRO=*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  found=1
  pid=${e#/proc/}; pid=${pid%/environ}
  d=$(printf '%s\n' "$env" | sed -n 's/^ROS_DOMAIN_ID=//p' | head -n 1)
  case "$d" in ""|0) echo "pid $pid: default DDS domain"; bad=1 ;; *[!0-9]*) echo "pid $pid: invalid ROS_DOMAIN_ID $d"; bad=1 ;; esac
done
[ "$found" -eq 1 ] || { echo "no running ROS 2 processes found"; exit 1; }
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Pick a site-unique domain ID (e.g. 42) and set ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42 in the launch environment of every node of the system, then restart them.

remediation.command:
set -u
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
tma_pkg_remove() { for p in "$@"; do

  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y purge "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n remove "$p"; fi; done; }

  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then dnf -y install "$p";
  elif command -v yum >/dev/null 2>&1; then yum -y install "$p";
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then apt-get -y install "$p";
  elif command -v zypper >/dev/null 2>&1; then zypper -n install "$p"; fi; done; }

tma_bak() { [ -e "$1" ] || return 0; ls "$1".tmaegis.bak.* >/dev/null 2>&1 || cp -a "$1" "$1.tmaegis.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"; return 0; }
